# skeuo.fm

> skeuo.fm turns a typed sentence into a real, working, skeuomorphic music player:
> an AI-generated player body (the "skin") wrapped around functional controls —
> play/pause, scrub, volume, transport — that drive real Spotify playback. Describe
> a player ("a translucent Bondi-blue iMac jukebox", "a Halo UNSC console", "a chrome
> cthulhu deck") and the pipeline paints the body, fits the controls to it, and hands
> you a player you can actually use.

## What it is

skeuo.fm is a generative skeuomorphism toy and tool. Skeuomorphism is interface
design that imitates the look and feel of real-world physical objects (brushed metal,
glass, knobs, LEDs). Here the skeuomorphic shell is generated from a text prompt by an
image model, then a layout step fits real, interactive music controls onto the painted
body so the result is a genuinely usable player, not a static picture. Playback is real
Spotify.

## How it works

- A text prompt describes the desired player body.
- An image model paints the skeuomorphic body (the "skin").
- A template + vision step masks and snaps real controls (play, scrub, volume) onto
  the painted body so they line up with the artwork.
- The finished player drives real Spotify playback in the browser.

## Notes

- skeuo = "skeuomorphic"; .fm = the music/radio top-level domain. Read as "skew-oh dot F M".
- Built by Conner Ward.
